title: An impact study of acoustic environment on users in large interior spaces
research_focus: To explore the influence of acoustic environment on people in eight large-scale spaces, divided into three functional categories, using grounded theory and questionnaires, and to identify common characteristics in subjective evaluation.

sample_context.description: 41 valid interviewees (29 temporary users, 12 staff), aged 9 to 72 years (median 32 years), male to female ratio almost 1:1. Participants were users and staff in large-scale public buildings.
sample_context.setting: Eight large-scale public buildings in Tianjin, China, categorized as traffic buildings (Tianjin East, West, South Railway Stations), exhibition buildings (Tianjin Meijiang Convention and Exhibition Center, Tianjin International Exhibition Center), and sports buildings (Tianjin University, Nankai University, Tianjin Olympic Sports Center Gymnasiums).

findings.description: The presence of high-level, pervasive background noise, often perceived as noisy and annoying, especially in crowded environments.
supporting_quotes: The environment here is noisier than that in Tianjin Exhibition Center

findings.antecedent: Large number of sound sources / Complicated acoustic environment
findings.description: The perception of many different sound sources contributing to a complex and sometimes overwhelming acoustic environment, making it hard to discern individual sounds.
supporting_quotes: I cannot figure out how many kinds of sounds here.

findings.antecedent: Acoustic environment characteristics (e.g., train passing, decoration area noise, sports sounds)
findings.consequent: Emotional change (e.g., anxiety, nervousness, annoyance, excitement, motivation)
findings.description: The acoustic environment directly influences emotional states, leading to both negative (anxiety, annoyance) and positive (excitement, motivation) emotional shifts depending on the context and individual perception.
supporting_quotes: The sound of the train passing by... makes me feel anxious.
All kinds of sounds can motivate me and inspire me to play more energetically.

findings.consequent: Negative feelings (e.g., tiredness, difficulty concentrating, feeling bad)
findings.description: A blend of various sounds creating a messy or complicated auditory experience, often leading to fatigue or discomfort.
supporting_quotes: The voice here is too complicated. There is messy sound.

findings.antecedent: Sensible sound with certain spectrum component (e.g., buzzing, sharp radio, children crying)
findings.theme_name: Sensible sound with certain spectrum component
findings.description: Specific, distinct sound components, particularly those with sharp or buzzing qualities, are perceived as uncomfortable or irritating.
supporting_quotes: I can hear the buzzing sound, which is distinct in my ear when I am quiet.
There are sharp broadcasting and sharp crying of children.

findings.consequent: Emotional effect (annoyance, anxiety, hurry, depression, excitement, happiness, motivation, brightness, relaxation)
findings.description: The acoustic environment significantly impacts users' emotional states, with negative effects (annoyance, anxiety) prevalent in traffic/exhibition buildings and positive effects (excitement, motivation) in sports buildings, influenced by spatial function.
supporting_quotes: I can hear the snoring when I am quiet, and this kind of sharp voice makes me uncomfortable and irritable.
All kinds of sounds can motivate me and inspire me to play more energetically.

findings.antecedent: Acoustic environment (noisy, sudden sounds, complicated voice)
findings.consequent: Influence on attention and thinking ability (distraction, inability to focus, decreased judgment/reaction speed)
findings.source: Influence on attention and thinking ability section
findings.theme_name: Influence on attention and thinking ability
findings.description: A noisy or complicated acoustic environment negatively affects users' attention, leading to distraction and reduced ability to think clearly or make judgments, especially over time.
supporting_quotes: Attention was affected during the process of introducing him this house...
The environment here is so noisy that I can't think.

findings.consequent: Behavior influence (e.g., desire to leave, desire for quiet, willingness to stay longer, play more aggressively)
findings.description: The acoustic environment influences user behavior, leading to avoidance (desire to leave, seek quiet) in negatively perceived spaces and approach (willingness to stay, engage) in positively perceived spaces.
supporting_quotes: It's inevitable that people have loud voices in this environment. But we don't like it. We want to leave early.
These voices motivate me to play more aggressively.

themes_or_constructs: Sensible sound with certain spectrum component
Influence on attention and thinking ability
supporting_quotes_or_evidence_snippets: I can hear the buzzing sound when I am quiet, and this kind of sharp voice makes me uncomfortable and irritable.
The sound of the train passing by spreads across the wall, which makes me feel anxious.
Mixed sound (in Tianjin Meijiang Convention and Exhibition Center) makes me tired.
If the environment is quiet, I can concentrate on thinking about my problems.
The environment here is so noisy that I can't think. Even I don't know what I want to buy in the end.
It's inevitable that people have loud voices in this environment. But we don't like it. We want to leave early.
The sound environment is very good, and it would be strange if everyone plays the ball without talking. I like this environment and I always come here.
derived_hypotheses: The acoustic environment in large interior spaces significantly impacts users' emotions, attention, thinking ability, and behavior.
The impact of the acoustic environment on users varies significantly across different spatial functions (e.g., traffic, exhibition, sports buildings).

Despite functional differences, common dimensions of influence (emotional, attentional/cognitive, behavioral) can be summarized for subjective evaluation of acoustic environments in large interior spaces.
mechanism_candidates: The suitability of sounds for a given spatial function (or users' 'taste') mediates the emotional evaluation of the acoustic environment.
The complexity and unpredictability of sound sources in large spaces contribute to cognitive load and distraction, affecting attention and thinking ability.
Chronic exposure to noisy or complicated acoustic environments can lead to a decrease in judgment and reaction speed over time.
The acoustic environment's perceived quality (positive vs. negative) drives approach-avoidance behaviors (e.g., willingness to stay longer vs. desire to leave early).
transferability_limits: The findings are based on studies in specific large public buildings in Tianjin, China, and may not be directly transferable to other cultural contexts, building types (e.g., residential, office), or smaller spaces.
The study focuses on temporary users and staff, and findings might differ for long-term occupants or different user groups.
limitations: The study primarily relies on subjective evaluation, and future research should explore the relationship between specific objective acoustic indicators and the identified impact aspects.
The questionnaire survey was conducted in eight case study sites, but the detailed analysis of acoustic environment evaluation within each function is planned for future discussion.

paper_metadata.title: An impact study of acoustic environment on users in large interior spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_title: An impact study of acoustic environment on users in large interior spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: As many large buildings have been built worldwide recently, it is necessary to study how the acoustic environment in those buildings affects people in order to improve the acoustical comfort in them. The aim of this study is to explore the influence of acoustic environment on people in eight large-scale spaces, which are divided into three categories according to function, through grounded theory, and questionnaire. The results showed that “loud background noise,” “large number of sound sources,” “emotional change,” “mixed sounds,” and “sensible sound with certain spectrum component” were people’s main evaluation to the acoustic environment in large-scale spaces. Based on respondents’ perception, the influence of the acoustic environment in large-scale spaces could be classified into the following three aspects: emotional effect, influence on attention, and influence on thinking ability and behavior. Although the evaluation of the acoustic environment varied widely with the difference in spatial functions, same perception dimensions could be summarized.
